info.title: MCP Redirection - Computer Use Agent Skill
info.description: Instructions for a computer use agent to use forwarded MCP tools (filesystem + fetch) exposed by an Amazon WorkSpaces Applications fleet with MCP Redirection (FORWARD_MCP_TOOLS) enabled.

servers.description: Windows Desktop with forwarded MCP servers on the host

post.summary: Find the forwarded tools in the tool list

steps: Inspect your available tools for names beginning with 'forwarded___'.
Match tools to a server by their described operation, not by exact spelling — separators may be normalized (dots become dashes for Bedrock).
tips: This fleet forwards two servers: 'filesystem' (read/write/list/move/info) and 'fetch' (URL retrieval).
If no 'forwarded___' tools exist, the stack is missing FORWARD_MCP_TOOLS or the image lacks the MCP servers — report it and stop.
x-agent-instructions.verification: You can name at least one forwarded filesystem tool and the forwarded fetch tool.

post.summary: List a directory via the forwarded filesystem server

steps: Call the forwarded list-directory tool with path 'C:\Users\Public\Documents'.
Read the returned entries directly from the tool result — no screenshot needed.
tips: The server is sandboxed to C:\Users\Public\Documents. Paths outside it return an error string.
Seeded files hello.txt and test.txt should appear.
x-agent-instructions.verification: The result lists directory entries with [FILE]/[DIR] prefixes.

post.summary: Read a file via the forwarded filesystem server

steps: Call the forwarded read-file tool with the full path, e.g. 'C:\Users\Public\Documents\hello.txt'.
The file contents are returned as text in the tool result.
tips: Prefer this over opening the file in an app and reading pixels — it is exact and cheap.
x-agent-instructions.verification: The tool result contains the file's text.

post.summary: Write a file via the forwarded filesystem server

steps: Call the forwarded write-file tool with 'path' and 'content' arguments.
Read the file back with the read-file tool to confirm.
tips: The server creates parent directories if needed and returns a byte count on success.
x-agent-instructions.verification: A subsequent read-file returns the content you wrote.

post.summary: Fetch a URL via the forwarded fetch server

steps: Call the forwarded fetch tool with a 'url' argument (e.g. 'https://example.com').
Optionally pass 'max_length' to cap the returned characters and 'start_index' to page through long content.
tips: HTML is converted to plain text for you. Use 'raw: true' only if you need the unconverted body.
This tool calls out to the public internet from the host — the fleet must have outbound network access.
x-agent-instructions.verification: The result contains readable text extracted from the page (e.g. the 'Example Domain' heading).

applicationOverview.name: Forwarded MCP Tools
applicationOverview.purpose: Call MCP servers running on the WorkSpaces host (filesystem, fetch) as ordinary agent tools, alongside desktop interaction tools.

x-agent-general-instructions.windowLayout: Not applicable — forwarded tools are headless API-style calls with structured arguments and text results. Desktop tools (screenshot/click/type) still control the visible screen.
interactionPatterns: Use forwarded tools for file and web operations: pass structured arguments (path, content, url) and read the text result directly.
Use desktop tools only for visual confirmation or GUI-only tasks.
Do not screenshot to read a forwarded tool's output — it is returned inline.

keyboardShortcuts.super+r: Open Run dialog (to launch Notepad for visual confirmation)

errorRecovery: 'Path outside allowed directories' → move the path inside C:\Users\Public\Documents and retry once.
No forwarded___ tools present → the fleet is not redirection-enabled; report and stop.
fetch errors (HTTP/URL) → the host may lack outbound internet; report the error string.
